sessions.title: Start here: the week
sessions.summary: How the five days run, the Polymex plant you will work on all week, the teams and the daily rhythm.

items.title: Your week
items.summary: What the week must produce, the days at a glance, the Polymex plant, teams and roles, house rules, setup and the exam.

items.title: Working with Claude: a one-pager
items.summary: How to prompt and use Claude for maximum efficiency: the five rules, a prompt template, a prompt that works for each session, and five ways to waste a session.

sessions.title: Day 1: The role
sessions.summary: What an FDE is and where the role comes from, then the consulting basics it relies on: structuring a message, navigating an organization, keeping the top-level view.

items.title: Day 1 pre-read
items.summary: Before the session: what the day looks like, the main terms (FDE, the last mile, OEE, answer first, sponsor) and the ideas to hold on to.

items.title: What an FDE is
items.summary: The job AI created: why deployment, not models, is where industrial AI fails, and what an FDE is accountable for. 122 slides.

items.title: Lab kit: Polymex Plant Pulse
items.summary: The morning lab: brief, rules for Claude Code, 90 days of shift logs and the data dictionary. Clone it and ship a dashboard.

items.title: Consulting skills 101
items.summary: Think like a partner, speak like one: structure the problem, structure the message, navigate the organization. 122 slides.

items.title: Afternoon exercises
items.summary: Five exercises on Polymex: turn Hervé's complaint into a testable problem, write an answer-first memo, adapt one message to four plant roles, design the target system, then brief Hervé live.

items.title: Session recording
items.summary: The session recordings, in the FDE School folder on Google Drive.

sessions.title: Day 2: The business
sessions.summary: Spotting problems worth solving: reading a P&L, an account's strategic position, field discovery, sizing impact in euros. Then leading an FDE project: impact-first scoping, governance, agile as practiced.

items.title: Day 1 main feedback
items.summary: The four points you raised on Day 1, and what changes: the end-to-end picture, real teamwork on one laptop, a pre-read for each day, and a Day 4 section on security, data and restricted stacks.

items.title: Day 2 pre-read
items.summary: Before the session: what the day looks like, the main terms (lean, the eight wastes, contribution margin, the five filters, project charter, baseline) and the ideas to hold on to.

items.title: The total view of an FDE project
items.summary: The ten minutes that open Day 2: the five phases of an FDE engagement, the FDE's role in each, and where each day of the week and each Polymex lab fits. 5 slides.

items.title: Problems worth solving
items.summary: How plants work, how lean measures them, and which gains reach the P&L; then choose where the Polymex group should start. 63 slides.

items.title: Polymex knowledge bundle
items.summary: The whole Polymex group in one folder: board memo, 2025 P&Ls of the group and its four plants, capacity, capex, bank covenant, sales, the lean program and 28 interviews. Download it for the morning lab and work with it all day.

items.title: Morning exercises
items.summary: Spot the waste in pairs, then the lab: read the Polymex knowledge bundle, choose which plant to start with and on which problem, and write a one-page memo to the CEO and COO.

items.title: Leading an FDE project
items.summary: The six-phase method, impact-first scoping, governance and the gains validation protocol. 36 slides.

items.title: Afternoon exercises
items.summary: Write the Polymex project charter from this morning's memo and the bundle, the Ferralux counting rules, and a validation protocol another team tests as the controller.

items.title: Session recording
items.summary: The session recordings, in the FDE School folder on Google Drive.

sessions.title: Day 3: The technology
sessions.summary: Planning at the Lyon plant, from the procedure to a running system: map the true process with data, choose one component per step (language model, decision model, rules engine, solver, a person), define what good looks like, then build the system on a platform and run it with the planner.

items.title: Day 2 main feedback
items.summary: The four points you raised on Day 2, and our answers: the intensity, pictures in the slides, the paperboard figures, and a one-pager on how to prompt Claude.

items.title: Day 3 pre-read
items.summary: Before the session: what the day looks like, the main terms (language and decision models, agents, ontology, rules engine, solver, the true process, human gates, five whys, entitlement) and the ideas to hold on to.

items.title: LLMs and agentic systems in 30 minutes
items.summary: What a language model is, what an agent really is, and what you build with them: which component for which step, and where people stay. 21 slides.

items.title: From the stated process to the target architecture
items.summary: What an AI system is really made of, the two maps (the current value stream and the future process), and how to define what good looks like. 43 slides; the six that answer the exercises are added after the session.

items.title: Lab kit: Lyon planning process
items.summary: The morning lab: the planning procedure, eight process-walk interviews, a day shadowing Corinne, four weeks of plan changes, the rules people apply, the platform catalogue and the templates. Open it in Claude Code.

items.title: Morning exercises
items.summary: Map the stated and the true planning process at Lyon, design the target architecture and the ontology, then write a five-line scorecard of what good looks like.

items.title: Exercise 2 output: what good looks like
items.summary: The reference scorecard for Lyon planning: five measures with baseline, best week, target, owner and guardrail, the gain in euros, and the one chart to show Hervé first.

items.title: The platform and the first loop
items.summary: The six layers around every model call, permissions, the core platform, then deployment, mini-apps, the improvement loop and five whys. 33 slides; the two that give the lab's results are added after the session.

items.title: Lab kit: Lyon planning v1
items.summary: The afternoon lab: the platform tools (rules engine, long and fast solvers, harness), week 20's orders, 110 rules, Monday's events and inbox, and the app you run with Corinne. Node.js 20, nothing to install.

items.title: Rule register: Lyon planning
items.summary: The 110 rules from the rules workshop of 6 May, by category, each with its source, owner and status. Read it before Exercise 4.

items.title: Afternoon exercises
items.summary: Wire the platform tools into your architecture (permissions, the long and the short loop, tests), then run the first full version with Corinne and find the rules you are missing.

items.title: Lyon Planner app
items.summary: The planning system, running: ontology, rules, planning, data sources, feedback, an editable scorecard and the architecture, on week 20. One instance per team, opened from every laptop. Node.js 18, nothing to install.

items.title: Session recording
items.summary: The session recordings, in the FDE School folder on Google Drive.

sessions.title: Day 4: The obstacles
sessions.summary: A half day, in the afternoon. Everything that goes wrong on an FDE project, technical and people, and your first 48 hours in eight real situations. Then scaling from Lyon to the group's three other plants: humility, owners, incentives, local culture, and IT from day one.

items.title: Day 3 main feedback
items.summary: The five points you raised on Day 3, and what changed: clearer exercise instructions, a Claude Code survival kit, data with traps, the link between theory and exercises, and the app-building part.

items.title: Day 4 pre-read
items.summary: Before the session: what the day covers, the main terms (data quality, legacy systems, resistance, change curve, champions, sponsors) and the ideas to hold on to.

items.title: What goes wrong, and how it scales
items.summary: The two families of obstacles, technical and people, the known moves for each, the first 48 hours, then five principles for scaling to a new plant. 30 slides; the one that sums up Exercise 1 is added after the session.

items.title: Exercises
items.summary: Eight situation cards: what you do in the next 48 hours when a sponsor goes silent, the data was wrong or people refuse the tool. Then a scale plan from Lyon to Haguenau, Évreux and Tarragona, on one poster.

items.title: Session recording
items.summary: The session recordings, in the FDE School folder on Google Drive.

sessions.title: Day 5: The full motion
sessions.summary: Five companies, disguised, one per team: a family-owned compounder, a sports brand, an appliance and cookware group, a pharmaceutical laboratory and a printer company. Each team opens a signed project with a kickoff document for the executive committee. Then the debrief, the operating principles, your 30/60/90-day plan and the FDE Certification exam.

items.title: Day 4 main feedback
items.summary: The four points you raised on Day 4, and what changed: shorter theory, more exercises in the morning, a real ontology shown, and a simple example of an ontology.

items.title: A simple ontology, step by step
items.summary: The ontology of a two-oven bakery in five steps, the same five steps at Lyon, a twenty-minute exercise, and where to see a real ontology in production.

items.title: Day 5 pre-read
items.summary: Before the session: how Friday runs, the main terms (pre-sales, kickoff, executive committee, baseline, kill criteria) and how to prepare for the exam.

items.title: The full motion: the kickoff
items.summary: The brief for Friday morning: five companies, one per team, and what a kickoff must tell an executive committee after pre-sales. 10 slides.

items.title: Case 1: Halden Polymers, a family-owned compounder
items.summary: Team 1. Scheduling at the lead vinyl plant. The company, its strategy, what pre-sales promised, the site data and the six people you present to.

items.title: Case 2: Peakline, a sports brand that makes what it sells
items.summary: Team 2. Fewer line stops from missing parts at its European bike plant, just before the peak season. The company, its strategy, what pre-sales promised, the site data and the committee.

items.title: Case 3: Groupe Ardent, small appliances and cookware
items.summary: Team 3. Less scrap on the coating lines of a French cookware plant. The company, its strategy, what pre-sales promised, the site data and the executive committee.

items.title: Case 4: Laboratoires Sorel, pharmaceuticals and dermo-cosmetics
items.summary: Team 4. Faster batch release at a dermo-cosmetics plant, under pharmaceutical rules. The company, its strategy, what pre-sales promised, the site data and the executive committee.

items.title: Case 5: Meridian Imaging, printers and document services
items.summary: Team 5. A higher first-time fix rate for field technicians, during an acquisition. The company, its strategy, what pre-sales promised, the site data and the executive committee.

items.title: Morning exercises
items.summary: The situation, the timing, the eight-slide kickoff template, the checklist and the questions the executive committee will ask.

items.title: Debrief, principles and the exam
items.summary: The debrief of the five kickoffs, the ten operating principles of the week, and the close. Added after the session.

items.title: Your 30/60/90 plan and exam rules
items.summary: The 30/60/90 template for your first deployment and the exam rules read aloud at 14:40.

items.title: Feedback on the week
items.summary: The end-of-week feedback form, ten minutes, before certificates. Answer on the site; your name is optional and only the trainers read the answers.

items.summary: The session recordings, in the FDE School folder on Google Drive.
